data.text/markdown:
Does California's new water rights data still say who holds each right?

The State Water Resources Control Board is retiring its old water rights system, eWRIMS, for a new one, CalWATRS. The old system's one-row-per-right file, the Water Rights LIST, is marked DISCONTINUED and "will be removed in the near future". The board says "you won't find a one-to-one replacement for this file". So far it has published two CalWATRS tables in its place: Participants (who is connected to each right) and Geospatial (each right's points of diversion, places of use and storage). Question. If you join the two CalWATRS tables, do you still get the facts the old file gave, above all who holds each right? Which fields are lost? And how stale is the old file really, given the portal says it was updated in November 2026? archive.py ran first. It downloaded all three datasets and their data dictionaries and saved the eWRIMS list as GeoParquet with checksums (outputs/archive_manifest.json). This notebook reads that archive.

data.text/markdown:
1. The old file

One row per right (a few IDs repeat; we keep the first). eWRIMS wrote the text NA for an empty value, so NA and blanks are treated as missing throughout.

Even the old file names a holder for only 80.3% of its 69,910 rights. Of the 13,775 without one, 88% are type "Not Determined" (13,204 rows, 19% of the file). Those rows rarely have an owner (8.5%), a location (1.7%) or a use (0.2%). They read as placeholder records, so results below are shown both for all rights and without them.

2. The strongest evidence against: does Participants already restore the holder?

The card expected the holder to be the big loss. The case against is the Participants table, created 2026-02-06: one row per link between a person or organization and a right, with a relationship type ("Primary owner", "Agent", "Non-primary owner"…) and an active or inactive status. If it names a holder for nearly every right, the loss is small and this becomes a crosswalk how-to. So check it first. Three tests per eWRIMS right:
  • Holder present: the right has at least one active "Primary owner" link.
  • Same party: the eWRIMS primary owner's party ID is one of the right's primary owner links (active or not). CalWATRS keeps the old eWRIMS party ID inside PARTICIPANT_CONVERSIONPAPID (A000084|434716 | …), so this is an exact check, not fuzzy name matching.
  • Same name: the active primary owner's name equals the eWRIMS name after upper-casing and dropping punctuation. CalWATRS rewrote many names in mixed case and added middle initials, so this undercounts.

data.text/markdown: The evidence against mostly holds. Participants names an active primary owner for 77.6% of all eWRIMS rights, and 96.6% of the 56,135 rights where eWRIMS named one. The holder is not lost; it moved to a second table that has to be joined on the right ID. Where eWRIMS named a holder, 97.8% of rights carry the same eWRIMS party into CalWATRS as a primary owner, and 62.1% have an active owner whose name matches letter for letter. The gap between the two is mostly rewritten names, not different holders. 2.2% of rights have an active owner added after eWRIMS's last update, so for those the old file is simply out of date. Of the 1,917 named-holder rights with no active CalWATRS owner, 66% are closed or inactive in eWRIMS: Closed 658, Inactive 612, Active 319, (blank) 133.

3. Join Geospatial and Participants on the right ID

Geospatial has one row per link between a right and a feature. eWRIMS listed one point of diversion per right (the most recently updated one) with its eWRIMS POD_ID, and CalWATRS keeps that ID as the first part of GR_CONVERSION_ID (6598|Point of Diversion). So point-of-diversion fields are compared on the very same point.

data.text/markdown:
4. The field crosswalk

Each eWRIMS column was read against the three data dictionaries and given the CalWATRS column that means the same thing, if there is one. The table below is that judgment; every eWRIMS column not listed has no CalWATRS equivalent. where says which CalWATRS rows a value comes from: right (Participants, right-level columns, repeated on every row), owner or agent (active primary owner or agent links), pod (the Geospatial row for the same point of diversion) or feature (any Geospatial row for the right). kind says how values are compared: text after upper-casing and dropping punctuation, dates by day, numbers to 6 significant digits (a zero counts as empty: eWRIMS wrote 0 face value on every statement), member if the eWRIMS value is one of a CalWATRS comma list. Status and type (vocab) use new terms and are scored in section 5. renamed fields hold the same fact in new words or new IDs and aren't scored; derived fields are counts or copies you can rebuild from the CalWATRS rows (number of points, uses, owners, petitions). same_value is the share agreeing among rights where both systems have a value.

data.text/markdown: 60 of 160 eWRIMS columns have a CalWATRS equivalent (plus the right ID). 99 have none, and 71 of those were filled for at least 5% of rights. By the data dictionary's own sections, most losses are per-use detail (population, stock, use acreage, seasons), application amounts and fees (MAX_DD_APPL, MAX_STORAGE…), GIS bookkeeping for the point (quad map, CalWater watershed, location method), licensing steps, and every enforcement field. Permit, license and certificate numbers, the parcel number, the project summary and the status history date are gone too. Point locations carry over: 99.9% of eWRIMS points are within 10 m of the same point in CalWATRS. Of the scored fields, priority date agrees for 100% of rights where both have it, face value for 100%, and the eWRIMS party ID for 100%.

5. Status and type: same facts, new words

CalWATRS renamed the status and type vocabulary. eWRIMS said a statement of diversion was type "Statement of Div and Use", status "Claimed"; CalWATRS says type "Riparian", status "Active". The WaDE rebuild spike (wade-water-rights-rebuild/) met the same problem and learned a lookup: for each CalWATRS combination, take the term most of its matched rights carried in WaDE's last California table. WaDE's terms are eWRIMS terms (WaDE appends the statement sub-type to the type), so that lookup is a CalWATRS → eWRIMS translation. Here we reuse it two ways:
  1. WaDE's lookup as it was, rebuilt with the WaDE spike's own helpers (imported from that folder, not edited) and the same keys: status on CalWATRS status + type, type on CalWATRS type + subtype. We score it against the eWRIMS file. On rights that were in WaDE that's in-sample; on the rest of eWRIMS (WaDE filtered out ended rights) it's a genuine out-of-sample test.
  2. The same method learned on the whole eWRIMS file, published as outputs/status_type_lookup.csv. It's in-sample, so its score is a ceiling.

data.text/markdown: Without a lookup, the same word appears in both systems for 47% of statuses and 30% of types. WaDE's lookup restores 93% of statuses and 96% of types on the rights it learned from. On eWRIMS rights WaDE never carried, the type lookup still holds (96%) but the status lookup gets only 10% right. Those rights are mostly inactive, revoked, cancelled or rejected, which WSWC's filter kept out of WaDE, so the lookup has no entry for 38% of them. For those statuses CalWATRS kept the eWRIMS word, so falling back to the CalWATRS word when the lookup has no entry lifts it to 38%. Learned on the whole eWRIMS file, the same method reaches 93% for status and 97% for type: an in-sample ceiling, not a forecast. The rest can't be told apart from CalWATRS's columns.

6. How stale is "last updated"?

data.text/markdown: The eWRIMS list's portal date, 2026-11-12, is the last edit to the dataset's metadata; its description now says it is discontinued and "hasn't been updated since July 2025". The CSV was re-uploaded 2026-10-01, its file name says 2025-08-05, and the newest change inside it is 2025-06-06. So "last updated" overstates its freshness by 524 days. The CalWATRS tables are what they say: uploaded this week, with records added within days of the download.

Result

  • Holder: kept, but moved. Participants names an active primary owner for 96.6% of the rights eWRIMS named one for, and carries the same eWRIMS party for 97.8%.
  • Fields: 61 of 160 eWRIMS columns have a CalWATRS equivalent; 99 don't.
  • Vocabulary: status and type need a lookup; the WaDE one doesn't transfer to rights it never saw.
  • Freshness: the old file's "last updated" is 524 days newer than its data.
